# Introduction

The search for the Higgs Boson represents a milestone in modern particle physics. Using deep learning to distinguish between signal and background processes has become an essential technique for improving discovery potential [@baldi2014searching].

# Methodology

We leverage the JAX ecosystem for its high-performance automatic differentiation and XLA-accelerated linear algebra [@jax2018github]. To handle the 11 million samples efficiently without straining systems with limited RAM, we utilize DuckDB [@duckdb2019] to stream data directly from Parquet files.

## The Model

We employ a 3-layer Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) with the following architecture:
- Layer 1: 256 units (ReLU)
- Layer 2: 128 units (ReLU)
- Layer 3: 64 units (ReLU)
- Output: 1 unit (Sigmoid)

# Preliminary Results

Initial training runs on the 21 low-level kinematic features show performance gains as the model depth increases. Full results are available on the [Dashboard](dashboard.qmd).
